channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77968-1

Electronic structure calculations usually need a good starting guess, often unavailable for strongly correlated systems. The authors develop an auto-initializing algorithm that efficiently finds accurate ground states from random Slater determinants.
item.dc:title: An auto-initializing algorithm to determine electronic ground states from random Slater determinants
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang
Matthew Otten

item.title: Religious celibacy is linked to marriage and wealth transmission practices across different world religions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78153-0

Lifelong religious celibacy has been linked to sibling competition over parental wealth. Here, the authors show that celibacy is linked to marriage patterns, and its prevalence among men and women is related to which sex faces higher marriage payments.
item.dc:title: Religious celibacy is linked to marriage and wealth transmission practices across different world religions
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Šaffa
Sara Sherbaji
Ruth Mace

item.title: Deep-learning single-cell profiling uncovers interbacterial and drug-driven reshaping of pathogen virulence
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77989-w

This study introduces MALVINA, a deep-learning platform that measures bacterial invasion and DNA damage in individual human cells, revealing how bacterial interactions and commonly used drugs reshape pathogen virulence.
item.dc:title: Deep-learning single-cell profiling uncovers interbacterial and drug-driven reshaping of pathogen virulence

item.title: Structural mechanisms underlying resistance to Switch-II pocket inhibitors in KRAS
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78133-4

This study explores how clinically observed KRAS resistance mutations alter drug-binding interactions and dynamics of the Switch-II pocket while preserving oncogenic signaling, providing a structural framework for developing more durable KRAS inhibitors.
item.dc:title: Structural mechanisms underlying resistance to Switch-II pocket inhibitors in KRAS

item.title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-q charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe2
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78072-0

The authors show that the subcomponents of the charge density wave in 1T-TiSe₂ are unequal and set in one by one, beginning with an unexpected unidirectional state.
item.dc:title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-q charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe2

item.title: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77673-z

Hydrogels with high deformation and resilience are desirable for applications such as injectable cardiac patches. Here, authors provide a strategy using chlorophyll as a physical crosslinker to engineer highly compressible hydrogels.
item.dc:title: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels

item.title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78263-9

The authors develop a domino catalytic system that dynamically reconstructs active sites’ electronic structure, lowering reaction barriers and inhibiting metal leaching for efficient and durable water purification.
item.dc:title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification
